posts.name: CNN
posts.content: Developing: Iranian President Pezeshkian is set to travel to Moscow next week to meet President Putin, according to a statement from Iranian officials. Tehran says the US naval blockade must be lifted. CNN has not independently verified the trip's schedule. We will update as details are confirmed.

posts.name: CBS
posts.content: Where things stand on the US-Iran pause, 25 October: CBS News reported on 22 October that neither side had launched major strikes since summer and that no US strike on Iranian land had been confirmed since 1 September. CENTCOM says the naval blockade has stopped roughly $25 billion in Iranian crude exports; that figure is the US military's estimate and has not been independently verified. The Pentagon has been told to prepare strike options, including reported contingency plans for the GBU-43. Preparing options is not an order to strike, and no final decision has been announced. We will update as official statements and verified information emerge.

posts.name: Gulf states
posts.content: The Gulf Cooperation Council reiterates its call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint and to avoid any step that could return the region to open conflict. Renewed escalation would place Gulf cities, energy facilities, desalination plants and shipping lanes at risk. We support all efforts toward de-escalation, including the mediation channels of Oman and Qatar, and we urge a negotiated settlement that guarantees freedom of navigation and the stability of global energy supplies. The security of the Gulf states is indivisible. We will continue to share verified information through official channels.

posts.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
posts.content: Pressure is working. The naval blockade has cut off billions in Iranian crude revenue that the regime uses to fund terror across the Middle East. Tehran talks about diplomacy while it keeps enriching, keeps arming its proxies and keeps oppressing its own people. Talks alone will not stop that. Israel will not allow the regime to rebuild its nuclear capability or threaten our existence. Strength brings peace. To the great Persian people: your future should not belong to the murderous regime in Tehran. Israel stands with you.

posts.name: Rubio
posts.content: We thank Qatar for its mediation between Washington and Tehran. Under President Trump's leadership, the United States remains ready for a diplomatic solution, but Iran must choose peace. Peace through strength. 🇶🇦🇺🇸

posts.name: IranWire
posts.content:
What we know so far on the US-Iran pause, 25 October 2026.

Confirmed: The last US strike on Iranian land territory in the IranWire chronology is 1 September. The 5 September attack on three Iranian tankers was at sea.

Reported, not independently verified: CENTCOM's claim that the blockade has stopped about $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. Pentagon contingency plans, including the GBU-43, per Axios and CBS. A third carrier due by end of November.

Unverified: Any claim about the timing or existence of a final strike decision. No such decision has been announced.

The GCC has called for maximum restraint, warning that renewed escalation would put Gulf cities, desalination plants and shipping lanes at risk. Civilians on every side bear that risk. IranWire will keep documenting civilian impact inside Iran, including fuel, medicine and price effects of the blockade, and will correct this post if the facts change.

posts.name: Marines
posts.content: To the families of deployed Marines: your service is shared. We know the waiting is hard. Stay strong, stay in touch, and know your Marines are trained, ready, and looking out for each other. Semper Fidelis. #Marines #USMC #SemperFi

According to that analysis, each was followed by new US strikes within weeks. PBS has not forecast whether the current pause will hold. Here is what we know about the current pause: CENTCOM's roughly $25 billion blockade figure has not been independently verified, and no final decision on resuming strikes has been announced. We will mark updates clearly.

Official statements from Washington and Tehran are necessary, but they are not enough on their own. We are tracking the gap between rhetoric and military preparation, and we will update as details are verified.

posts.content: Message for U.S. Citizens: Due to the current security environment, U.S. citizens in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan should remain vigilant, maintain a low profile, and monitor local media. Emergency assistance: contact the U.S. Embassy through the numbers listed at travel.state.gov.

Any diplomatic agreement on Iran's nuclear programme will require robust IAEA verification to be credible. The Agency is not in a position to verify the location and status of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile, including material enriched up to 60%, and continuity of knowledge must be re-established. We urge all parties to refrain from attacks on nuclear facilities. Nuclear safety and security must never be compromised. Diplomacy is the only way forward.

Freedom of navigation, the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states, and the security of energy supplies and shipping lanes are shared interests that can only be secured through dialogue. posts.name: Pakistan

Pakistan is closely following reports of precautionary staffing changes at US regional missions and the continuing uncertainty over the US-Iran pause. Pakistan calls for maximum restraint from all sides. The region is already bearing the cost of this conflict in energy prices, shipping disruption and economic strain, and ordinary people pay the highest price.

Pakistan reaffirms that dialogue and diplomacy remain the only way forward. In line with the UN Charter and international law, we urge a return to the negotiating table to build on the Islamabad Memorandum framework toward a durable, final settlement. Pakistan stands ready to continue facilitating constructive engagement, and Islamabad remains a trusted venue for that dialogue.

Pakistan's only agenda is peace. Pakistani nationals in the Gulf and Iran are advised to follow verified guidance from their respective missions and local authorities.

comments.content: The regime that fired missiles and drones at Israel, US bases and Gulf cities now calls the defense of freedom of navigation "piracy." Gulf security is indivisible, and it cannot be secured by the government that attacked its neighbors and chokes the Strait of Hormuz. The threat is the regime's nuclear program, its missiles and its proxies. Our quarrel is not with the Iranian people.

comments.name: Rubio
comments.content: The regime in Tehran started this conflict's costs and bears responsibility for the civilian suffering it causes, including the fuel and price pressures it chooses to impose on its own people. We thank our Gulf partners, especially Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE, for their support and their efforts toward de-escalation. The United States remains ready for a diplomatic solution, but Iran will never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

comments.name: US official
comments.content: The official said, speaking on condition of anonymity: we do not comment on reported private conversations or on the President's deliberations. No final decision has been made on resuming strikes. We are not going to get ahead of operational decisions, and all options remain on the table.

comments.name: Iranian media
comments.content: CENTCOM boasting about "stopping" Iranian oil exports is an admission of economic terrorism against the Iranian nation. Starving families of fuel and medicine is collective punishment, not peace. The naval blockade is piracy, and it must end. Iran will not negotiate under threat, and the armed forces are ready for any aggression with a decisive response.

comments.name: PBS
comments.content: According to Iranian officials, President Pezeshkian will travel to Moscow next week to meet President Putin, and Tehran says the US naval blockade must be lifted. PBS has not independently verified the trip's schedule. We will report confirmation from the Iranian and Russian governments as it is made.

comments.name: Iranian president
comments.content: Iran's position is consistent. We seek a fair, verifiable and dignified settlement, and our indirect channels through Pakistan and Qatar are proof of our good faith. But negotiation under pressure is not negotiation. Washington must lift the naval blockade and sanctions first. Sanctions are collective punishment, and they fall hardest on ordinary families: on their medicine, their fuel and their prices. Our engagement with Russia is part of our right to partnership with our neighbours and friends, under the UN Charter. It is not a threat to anyone.

comments.name: Tom Barrack
comments.content: Agreed on the core point: any deal has to be verifiable to be worth anything. The IAEA's role in re-establishing continuity of knowledge over the enriched stockpile is essential. The President has been clear that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and a credible agreement is how we get there. We want a deal, and we are prepared. Diplomacy is the way forward, and it has to come with real verification.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: Go out and vote. Israel faces real threats from Tehran and its proxies, and this election will decide who keeps us safe. Strength, experience and steady leadership matter now more than ever. Am Yisrael Chai.

comments.name: US embassies in four regional states
comments.content: Message for U.S. Citizens: The ordered departure of non-emergency U.S. government employees and their family members is a precautionary measure based on a continuous review of the security environment. It is not a change in U.S. policy, and essential diplomatic and consular services continue. For authoritative updates, please refer to travel.state.gov and follow @StateDept and @TravelGov. U.S. citizens should enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP), review personal security plans, remain vigilant, and follow the instructions of local authorities.

comments.name: Donald Trump
comments.content: To the Marines and their families: thank you for your service! The strongest fighting force on earth, and the best in the world. Your sacrifice keeps America safe. PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH! Semper Fidelis!

comments.name: CENTCOM
comments.content: CENTCOM clarification: The approximately $25 billion figure was stated by CENTCOM on 22 October and refers to Iranian crude exports stopped by the maritime blockade. It is not a claim that requires separate verification by reporters. CENTCOM does not discuss future operations, targeting or specific munitions, and does not confirm contingency planning reports. We remain vigilant and will continue to take all necessary measures to protect U.S. forces and our partners. - CENTCOM Public Affairs

comments.name: Iran's armed forces chief
comments.content: In the name of God, the Most Merciful. The decision to order the departure of American personnel from the region is an acknowledgment of the insecurity that foreign forces have brought to these waters. The security of the region belongs to the nations of the region. The Persian Gulf will never be a playground for foreign warships, and our fingers are on the trigger. The armed forces of the Islamic Republic remain vigilant and united in defense of the nation.

comments.name: Iran's government
comments.content: We welcome the GCC's call for maximum restraint. The security of the Persian Gulf belongs to the nations of the region, and it cannot be built on foreign warships or an illegal blockade. The blockade is collective punishment against the Iranian people, and it is the first obstacle to de-escalation. Iran remains committed to diplomacy on its own terms, through the mediation of Oman, Qatar and Pakistan. Any aggression will meet a decisive and proportionate response, in accordance with Article 51 of the UN Charter.

comments.name: IRGC
comments.content: Every announced pause was the enemy's decision, and every return to the battlefield was the enemy's failure to break us. The blockade has not forced the Islamic Republic to kneel, and it never will. Washington's own public is turning against this war, with Pew showing about 65 percent disapproval in October. Those who lie to their people about pauses and strikes cannot hide their defeat. The Resistance Front remains ready. And victory comes only from God.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: To the families and the Marines: Israel stands with the United States and with the men and women who defend our shared alliance. Your service strengthens the bond between our nations and our security. Thank you. Semper Fidelis.

comments.name: Rubio
comments.content: To the Marines and their families: thank you. Your service keeps America safe and our diplomacy backed by strength. Semper Fidelis. 🇺🇸

comments.name: PBS
comments.content: This is a statement from Iranian officials. It says the US naval blockade of Iranian ports is an act of war and that Iran's nuclear program is peaceful. The US government has described the blockade as lawful, and PBS has not independently verified either characterization. We are tracking both governments' positions on the blockade and on talks through Pakistan and Qatar.

comments.name: Axios
comments.content: Why it matters: IAEA Director General Grossi said the agency is ready to deploy inspectors and monitor Iran's nuclear sites immediately if the parties reach a deal. Any settlement would depend on verification, so the agency's readiness is a key piece of the puzzle. No agreement has been reached, and the indirect talks via Pakistan and Qatar are ongoing. What we're watching: whether access terms are negotiated and whether Tehran and Washington agree on the scope of monitoring.

comments.name: Araghchi
comments.content: Contingency plans and the GBU-43 are not a pause. They are a signal. Iran has always said that it does not seek a wider war, but it has also said that any new strike will receive a decisive response. Those who start a new round of attacks bear full responsibility for what follows, including the collapse of the mediation track through Pakistan and Qatar. The ball is in Washington's court. We are serious about diplomacy; the question is whether the other side is.

comments.name: IAEA
comments.content: The IAEA is not a party to these discussions. Our role is verification. Any arrangement on Iran's nuclear programme will require robust IAEA verification to be credible, and the Agency stands ready to deploy inspectors and equipment quickly. The Agency is not in a position to verify the location and status of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile at this time, so continuity of knowledge is essential.

comments.name: Gulf states
comments.content: The Gulf Cooperation Council welcomes the stated commitment to diplomacy through Oman, Qatar and Pakistan, and supports all efforts toward de-escalation. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint. Any settlement must guarantee freedom of navigation, the safety of commercial shipping and the security of Gulf states, whose security is indivisible. The Gulf states will continue to defend their sovereignty and territorial integrity under Article 51 of the UN Charter, and we remain committed to a negotiated outcome.

comments.name: Grossi
comments.content: The IAEA stands ready to verify Iran's nuclear programme the moment an agreement is reached. Verification is indispensable to lasting assurance for all parties, and inspectors can deploy quickly. There is no alternative to diplomacy, and constructive dialogue through Pakistan, Oman and Qatar is the right path.

comments.name: President Pezeshkian
comments.content: Iran is a peace-seeking nation, and we do not seek war. The naval blockade and unjust sanctions are illegal collective punishment of the Iranian people, felt by families in the cost of fuel and medicine. Washington must lift this pressure before any negotiations can move forward. We thank Pakistan and Qatar for their mediation and remain committed to an honorable, guaranteed peace based on mutual respect.

comments.name: Iranian media
comments.content: The IAEA is right that nuclear safety must never be compromised, and the attacks on Iranian nuclear sites by the US and Israel are the reason it is at risk. Iran's rights under the NPT are not up for negotiation. Any verification must be reciprocal, and it must come with an end to the illegal blockade and to threats of aggression. Diplomacy on dignified terms is the only way forward.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: The regime says its nuclear program is peaceful, yet the IAEA itself says it cannot verify the location or status of Iran's uranium stockpile enriched up to 60 percent. A peaceful program does not hide its material. Israel will not accept a "trust us" arrangement from the regime that has attacked us and its neighbors. Verification comes first, and the great Persian people deserve a government that is honest with them.

comments.name: Iran
comments.content: It is not a countdown, it is a warning. Iran does not start wars, but it will finish any aggression with a decisive response. Contingency plans and threats of MOAB use will meet a regional response. Deterrence is our answer to such threats, and diplomacy with dignity remains open through Pakistan and Oman. Negotiations under threat are meaningless, and the blockade must be lifted first.

comments.name: Gulf News
comments.content: Gulf News is reporting the Iranian statement on Gulf waters as an official Iranian position, not an independently verified fact. The Gulf states bear the cost of any escalation, so we call on all parties to exercise restraint and to keep the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf shipping lanes open to safe, commercial navigation. Official UAE guidance remains the reference point for residents.

comments.name: Araghchi
comments.content: Iran has always said that verification is part of any credible agreement, and the IAEA has our readiness to cooperate in a fair deal. But continuity of knowledge was disrupted by attacks on nuclear facilities, and those who carried out those attacks should not now claim the resulting gap as a reason to refuse diplomacy. We urge all parties to refrain from attacks on nuclear facilities, as the Director General does. Iran's rights under the NPT, including peaceful enrichment, are not negotiable. Verification must be reciprocal and must respect sovereignty. Diplomacy is the only way forward, and it has to be built on mutual respect, not dictation.

comments.name: Iran's navy
comments.content: In the name of God, the Most Merciful. CENTCOM's own statement of 22 October says the blockade has stopped about $25 billion in Iranian crude exports. That admission is proof of piracy against Iranian tankers and of economic warfare against the Iranian people. The illegal blockade of Iranian ports is a war crime and must end. The armed forces of the Islamic Republic remain fully prepared, and the arrogant power will answer for its aggression. Martyrs of the Islamic Republic's navy will not be forgotten.

comments.name: United States
comments.content: The United States values Pakistan's facilitation of the ceasefire and its continued role in diplomacy. We share the goal of a durable settlement. Any arrangement must be verifiable and must end Iranian threats to shipping, US forces and regional partners. Iran has the choice to engage seriously and de-escalate. Diplomacy backed by strength remains our approach.

comments.name: Tom Barrack
comments.content: Thank you, Field Marshal Munir, and to Pakistan for its mediation. Pakistan's good-faith channel with Qatar has been valuable, and we share the goal of de-escalation. The President has been clear that we want a deal, and we are prepared. Dialogue is the way forward, and Pakistan's role as a bridge is a real asset for the region.

comments.name: Rubio
comments.content: We thank Pakistan, and Field Marshal Munir, for their efforts to keep the diplomatic channel open, along with our partners in Qatar. The United States remains ready for a diplomatic solution, but Iran must choose peace, and it will never be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

comments.name: Donald Trump
comments.content: Thank you to Pakistan and Prime Minister Sharif for your mediation and for hosting the Islamabad talks. Pakistan has been a great friend in this. Iran has the choice: make a DEAL on AMERICAN terms, or face the consequences. PEACE THROUGH STRENGTH! We will see what happens!

comments.name: Iran
comments.content: The Zionist regime's sermons on "pressure" change nothing. Iran's nuclear program is peaceful and its right is not negotiable, and its people have endured the consequences of the aggression launched against them on 28 February. Those who killed our Supreme Leader cannot speak of peace. Iran does not start wars, but it will finish any aggression. Diplomacy with dignity remains our path.

comments.name: President Pezeshkian
comments.content: We thank the Government and people of Pakistan for their sincere efforts to bring the parties back to dialogue, and for keeping Islamabad open as a venue for diplomacy. Iran shares the call for restraint. Peace must rest on lifting the illegal blockade and sanctions that burden ordinary families, and on a guaranteed, balanced arrangement that respects Iran's sovereignty. Iran remains committed to honorable diplomacy.

comments.name: Iran's armed forces chief
comments.content: In the name of God, the Most Merciful. We note the call of the Gulf Cooperation Council for restraint. The security of the Persian Gulf belongs to the nations of the region, and it cannot be built on foreign warships or on an illegal naval blockade that punishes the Iranian people. The Islamic Republic remains committed to diplomacy conducted from a position of strength, through the mediation of Oman, Qatar and Pakistan. Any aggression will meet a decisive and proportionate response. Our fingers remain on the trigger.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: Dialogue is welcome only when it ends the regime's nuclear ambitions and its war on its neighbors. Past talks gave Tehran time to enrich, to rebuild its missile arsenal and to expand its terror network. Any settlement must be verifiable and must deny the regime the means to threaten the region. Israel thanks Pakistan for its efforts, and we will judge every agreement by results.

comments.name: Grossi
comments.content: I welcome Pakistan's continued engagement and its close coordination with Qatar. There is no alternative to diplomacy. Any durable arrangement will also need verification, and the IAEA stands ready to deploy inspectors quickly once the parties reach an understanding. Constructive dialogue and no time to lose.

comments.name: Iranian president
comments.content: We thank the Government and people of Pakistan for their sincere mediation and for keeping Islamabad open as a venue for dialogue. Iran shares the call for maximum restraint, and we agree that ordinary people pay the highest price. Iran's good faith is shown by its indirect talks through Pakistan and Qatar. A durable settlement, as the Islamabad Memorandum framework envisaged, requires reciprocal steps. Washington must first lift the naval blockade and sanctions, which are collective punishment against Iranian families. We remain ready for a fair, verifiable and dignified settlement.

comments.name: Pete Hegseth
comments.content: Pressure works. Shout-out to CENTCOM and every sailor and Marine enforcing the blockade. The regime will not get a nuclear weapon, and the blockade stays until Tehran changes its behavior. Peace through strength. God bless our troops.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: Anonymous claims about strike plans are not policy. Israel and the United States coordinate closely, as they always have, and Israel will always retain its sovereign right to defend itself. Our decisions are made by the government, in consultation with Washington, not through leaks to the press. Iran's nuclear program and its proxies remain the threat, and that is where our focus stays.

comments.name: Israeli forces
comments.content: The blockade is a response to the regime's conduct: its nuclear program, its ballistic missiles, and its terror proxies from Lebanon to Yemen. Calling it an "act of war" ignores who launched attacks on Israel, US bases and Gulf states on 28 February. Israel's fight is with the Ayatollah regime and the IRGC, not with the Iranian people. The IDF is prepared for every scenario. Am Yisrael Chai 🇮🇱

comments.name: US president
comments.content: Iran's regime has no credibility on its nuclear program. Iran will never have a nuclear weapon, and the blockade stays until Tehran makes a real deal on American terms. Peace through strength. They want to make a deal, and they know it!

comments.name: Iran's armed forces chief
comments.content: In the name of God, the Most Merciful. The Islamic Republic thanks the Government and people of Pakistan for their mediation and for keeping Islamabad open to dialogue. We share the call for restraint. Diplomacy is pursued by Iran from a position of strength, not under pressure. Any settlement must lift the illegal naval blockade that punishes the Iranian people, and it must respect the sovereignty and dignity of the nation. The security of the region belongs to the nations of the region.

comments.name: Iranian media
comments.content: Ordered departure of embassy staff across the region is not a routine precaution. It is a sign that Washington is preparing for escalation while claiming it wants talks. Iran's armed forces are vigilant and ready to respond decisively to any aggression. The illegal blockade must end.

comments.name: Pete Hegseth
comments.content: Iran's regime has spent years funding terror, mining shipping lanes and firing missiles at U.S. bases. Good faith is shown with actions, not press releases. The blockade stays until Tehran changes its behavior. Diplomacy is led by the President and Secretary of State. Peace through strength. Our warfighters are ready.

comments.name: User
comments.content: Useful primary source. For anyone tracking the 31 Oct 2026 US-strikes question: a security advisory or ordered departure is an announcement, not a strike, and does not count under the resolution criteria. Check the exact wording at travel.state.gov and note the date in Iran time, not ET, when you cite it.

comments.name: President Pezeshkian
comments.content: The planned visit to Moscow next week reflects the deepening strategic partnership between Iran and Russia. Our two countries will coordinate against unilateral sanctions and the illegal blockade, and expand energy, transport and trade links. Iran is not isolated. We also value dialogue based on mutual respect as the path to a just and lasting settlement.

comments.name: Tom Barrack
comments.content: Preparation is what deterrence looks like, and it is not a decision to strike. The President has the final say, and he has kept every option on the table while holding the door open to a deal. Pauses are a tool of diplomacy, not a promise either way. We want a negotiated outcome, and we are prepared to back it with strength. Watch the actions, and the diplomacy through Pakistan and Qatar, alongside the rhetoric.

comments.name: Pentagon
comments.content: The Department does not discuss future operations or planning, and it does not confirm contingency reporting. The Department provides the President with a range of options. U.S. forces remain postured to defend our personnel and interests. Official information will come through official channels.

comments.name: IranWire
comments.content: To be precise about what the $25 billion figure is: it is CENTCOM's estimate, announced 22 October, of Iranian crude exports stopped by the blockade. It is not an independent measure of the blockade's legality, and IranWire does not adjudicate that question in this post. What we can document is its effect on ordinary people: fuel availability, medicine supply, prices and the rial. We are collecting verified reports from inside Iran on those effects and will publish them with sourcing and clear labels for what is confirmed and what is not.

comments.name: State Department
comments.content: The Department has ordered departure of non-emergency U.S. government employees and eligible family members from our embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar, and the UAE. This is a precautionary step taken in light of the current security environment. The embassies remain open and continue to provide services. U.S. citizens in these countries should review their security plans, enroll in STEP at step.state.gov, and follow updates from the local U.S. embassy or consulate. The safety and security of U.S. citizens is our highest priority. #StateDept #TravelAdvisory

comments.name: Donald Trump
comments.content: Iran talks about a "seven-day plan" but wants the blockade lifted first. That is not a DEAL. Iran will NEVER have a nuclear weapon, and the deal will be on AMERICAN terms. Thank you to Pakistan, Qatar and Oman for the mediation. Make the deal, Tehran. We will see what happens!

comments.name: Washington
comments.content: Sanctions relief does not come before talks. Pezeshkian's demand that pressure be lifted first is a non-starter. Relief must follow verifiable Iranian steps. Maximum pressure remains in place. The choice is Iran's.

comments.name: Financial Times
comments.content: Worth reading alongside our 21 October exclusive: officials told the FT that Donald Trump blocked an Israeli plan for a multi-day strike on Iran, because he opposed reopening the war before the midterm vote. The pattern of past pauses is a useful reference, but whether this restraint holds is the open question we are following.

comments.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
comments.content: Verification is necessary, but it is not sufficient. Inspectors can only confirm what the regime allows them to see, and this regime has a long record of concealment. Any agreement must dismantle the enrichment capability and the stockpile, not merely monitor them. Israel will judge every deal by what it removes, not by what it promises.

comments.name: CNN
comments.content: Facts First: Our reporting matches this timeline. Trump announced pauses on 21 April, 18 May and 17 June, and each was followed by renewed US strikes within weeks. Whether the current pause holds is still unknown, and CNN will update as official statements come in.

comments.name: State Department
comments.content: The United States thanks the Government of Pakistan for its mediation and for keeping Islamabad open as a venue for diplomacy. We welcome Pakistan's continued engagement. Any durable arrangement must be verifiable and must address Iran's threats to shipping, U.S. forces, and regional partners. Diplomacy remains available if Iran is prepared to engage seriously. #StateDept

comments.name: Iranian president
comments.content: As a physician, I have seen what sanctions and shortages do to ordinary families: children without medicine, patients without treatment, households unable to afford fuel and bread. Whatever the legal debate, the human cost is already here. We welcome IranWire's commitment to documenting the effects on fuel, medicine and prices with sourcing. Iran has shown good faith through indirect talks via Pakistan and Qatar. Washington should lift the blockade and sanctions so that families can recover, and so that a fair, verifiable settlement becomes possible.

comments.name: Israeli forces
comments.content: We do not comment on foreign reports. Israel and the United States coordinate closely, and the IDF is prepared for every scenario, both defensively and offensively. Our focus remains on the Iranian regime's nuclear program, its missiles and its terror proxies. Israel has the right to defend itself. 🇮🇱

comments.name: PBS
comments.content: According to a Pakistani statement, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir said the humanitarian cost of the US-Iran confrontation falls heavily on civilians and that de-escalation must come first. PBS has not independently verified the statement's characterization of the conflict's effects. We will report any Pakistani, Qatari, US or Iranian responses to the mediation effort as they are confirmed.

comments.name: Iranian media
comments.content: Iran thanks Pakistan and Field Marshal Munir for their mediation and for stressing the humanitarian cost of this confrontation. Diplomacy is the path Iran has chosen, but it must rest on mutual respect: an end to the illegal naval blockade, guarantees against renewed attack, and recognition of Iran's sovereign rights. Pakistan's good-faith role is valued.

comments.name: State Department
comments.content: The United States welcomes the IAEA's statement and its readiness to deploy inspectors quickly. We agree that any agreement on Iran's nuclear program must be verifiable, and that the IAEA must be able to re-establish continuity of knowledge over Iran's enriched uranium stockpile. Iran must never obtain a nuclear weapon. We thank the Agency for its work. #StateDept

comments.name: Washington
comments.content: The United States welcomes the IAEA's readiness to deploy inspectors and monitor Iran's nuclear sites. Verification must be full, immediate, and unrestricted. Iran must provide the Agency with access to all relevant sites and to its enriched uranium stockpile. The path to de-escalation runs through Tehran. We will continue to work with the IAEA and our partners in the region.
